process_area.title: Recall Initiation, Risk Assessment & Regulatory Notification

value_stream.name: Product Recall & Safety Corrective Action Management

fields.Participants: Product Safety Mgr, Quality, Customer Service, Vendor Mgmt, Legal, Store Ops
fields.Trigger: Safety complaint, regulator alert, vendor notice, or field incident
fields.Volume: ~30–60 issues triaged; ~3–8 escalate to formal recall

workflows.name: Product Safety Issue Intake, Triage & Hazard Classification

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "logs safety issue in recall case system" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-assign of "assigns preliminary severity" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-issue of "issue is isolated or systemic" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-496 (ensure controlled execution — Recall Initiation, Risk Assessment & Regulatory Notification (PA-89.1).)
- operational: mandatory hazard-classification field and dedicated triage queue; operational: hazard-classification field and dedicated triage queue
Pain Points / Risks: - **Detection risk**: Safety issues lost in generic complaint queues; mitigated by mandatory hazard-classification field and dedicated triage queue
System Touchpoints: - Recall case management; quality non-conformance module; item/lot/serial master; vendor master linkage

steps.activity: Customer Service / Store Ops / Quality logs safety issue in recall case system (source, SKU, lot, incident description, photos, injury/property damage flag)

Product Safety Mgr triages and classifies hazard (electrical/fire, chemical/toxic, mechanical/laceration, structural/failure, labeling/allergen) and assigns preliminary severity (Class I–III per Consumer Act / DTI-BPS)
Quality/Vendor Mgmt confirms affected SKU, lot, vendor, and whether the issue is isolated or systemic; duplicates against existing open recalls

fields.Participants: Product Safety Mgr, Quality, Legal, Merchandising, Insurance, DPO
fields.Trigger: Triaged issue flagged Class I/II or systemic

workflows.name: Recall Risk Assessment & Corrective Action Decision

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documents likelihood of regulatory mandatory action" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Recall Committee reviews assessment" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: documented severity matrix and committee review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-reaction risk**: Classifying a serious hazard as lower-tier; mitigated by documented severity matrix and committee review
System Touchpoints: - Risk assessment template; decision/authority log; document repository

steps.activity: Product Safety Mgr performs risk assessment: probability of harm × severity × exposure (units in market, time since sale); documents likelihood of regulatory mandatory action
Legal/Insurance assesses liability, product-liability exposure, and policy notification triggers; DPO screens affected-customer data needed for notification
Recall Committee reviews assessment; decides corrective action type (full recall, stop-sale, field repair, consumer notice, no-action); documents rationale and decision authority

fields.Participants: Regulatory Officer, Product Safety Mgr, Legal, Tax/Records

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prepares and files notification with DTI-BPS" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Legal/Regulatory notifies relevant LGUs and, for imports, Bureau of" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "Records Mgr retains regulatory correspondence and filings per BIR/SEC 10-year…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-496 (ensure controlled execution — Recall Initiation, Risk Assessment & Regulatory Notification (PA-89.1).)
- operational: compliance calendar and pre-cleared templates
Pain Points / Risks: - **Compliance risk**: Late or incomplete regulator notification triggers penalties; mitigated by compliance calendar and pre-cleared templates
System Touchpoints: - Regulatory filing portal integration; records retention; compliance calendar

steps.activity: Regulatory Compliance Officer prepares and files notification with DTI-BPS (consumer product safety) and/or FDA (regulated goods), within mandated timelines, including product, hazard, scope, and remedy
steps.duration: Per filing (<48 hr for mandatory, per the W1618 convention)

steps.activity: Legal/Regulatory notifies relevant LGUs and, for imports, Bureau of Customs and country-of-origin regulators; confirms any PS/ICC mark suspension
Records Mgr retains regulatory correspondence and filings per BIR/SEC 10-year and Consumer Act retention rules

fields.Participants: Supply Planning, Quality, Merchandising, IT, Store Ops, Ecommerce

workflows.name: Recall Strategy, Scope & Lot/Shipment Traceability Definition

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Merchandising/Supply Planning sets recall strategy" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-496 (ensure controlled execution — Recall Initiation, Risk Assessment & Regulatory Notification (PA-89.1).)
- operational: full chain-of-custody traceability and IT-assisted queries
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scope risk**: Incomplete lot/trace data leaves affected units in market; mitigated by full chain-of-custody traceability and IT-assisted queries
System Touchpoints: - Lot/serial/shipment traceability; inventory & sales history; omnichannel order history; recall scope record

steps.activity: Supply Planning defines recall scope: affected SKU(s), lots/batches, date ranges, receiving locations (DCs, stores), and sales channel exposure (in-store, ecommerce, marketplace, B2B)

IT/Supply Planning traces affected lots/serials through inventory and sales history (DC receipts, store transfers, POS sales, ecommerce orders, trade/gov deliveries) to quantify units in-field vs. on-hand
Merchandising/Supply Planning sets recall strategy: full retrieval, consumer replacement, refund, or repair; defines remedy matrix and recovery logistics

fields.Participants: VP Legal & Compliance, COO, CMO, CIO, Product Safety, Quality, Supply Chain, LP, Finance, HR/Comms

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-assign of "assigns incident commander" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "Committee sets recall KPIs and status reporting" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinates internal and external spokesperson, media holding statement, and store/DC staff briefing script" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-496 (ensure controlled execution — Recall Initiation, Risk Assessment & Regulatory Notification (PA-89.1).)
- operational: pre-defined activation authority and standing committee roster
Pain Points / Risks: - **Coordination risk**: Slow committee activation delays response; mitigated by pre-defined activation authority and standing committee roster
System Touchpoints: - Incident command / war-room tooling; status dashboard; communication broadcast (links to VS-63)

steps.activity: VP Legal & Compliance activates Recall Committee; confirms roles, decision authority, and cadence (daily war-room for high-severity); assigns incident commander
Committee sets recall KPIs and status reporting: units recovered vs. in-field, % notification reach, customer contact rate, SLA to resolution
Comms/HR coordinates internal and external spokesperson, media holding statement, and store/DC staff briefing script

fields.Participants: Vendor Mgmt, Merchandising, Legal, Quality, Finance

workflows.name: Vendor / Manufacturer Coordination & Corrective Action Agreement

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "Vendor Mgmt formally notifies vendor/manufacturer of recall decision" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Legal/Vendor Mgmt negotiates and executes corrective action agreement covering" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-496 (ensure controlled execution — Recall Initiation, Risk Assessment & Regulatory Notification (PA-89.1).)
- operational: purchase contract recall/indemnification clauses and documented evidence package
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-recovery risk**: Vendor disputes liability; mitigated by purchase contract recall/indemnification clauses and documented evidence package
System Touchpoints: - Vendor portal; contract/agreement repository; vendor scorecard linkage (links to VS-67)

steps.activity: Vendor Mgmt formally notifies vendor/manufacturer of recall decision; demands corrective action, cost responsibility, and root-cause report
Legal/Vendor Mgmt negotiates and executes corrective action agreement covering recovery logistics, reimbursement (refund + recall costs), and remedy supply (replacements)
Quality/Vendor Mgmt agrees vendor CAPA (design change, QA process change) and sets timeline for requalification of corrected product per W447 (DTI-BPS certification)

fields.Participants: Product Safety Mgr, Quality, Data Analytics, Store Ops

workflows.name: Recall Effectiveness Check Planning & Sample Design

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Product Safety Mgr defines effectiveness-check criteria" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System continuous audit of "Data Analytics/Store Ops designs audit sample" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "documents effectiveness results" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-496 (ensure controlled execution — Recall Initiation, Risk Assessment & Regulatory Notification (PA-89.1).)
- operational: quantitative effectiveness targets and independent sampling
Pain Points / Risks: - **Effectiveness risk**: Recall declared complete while units remain in market; mitigated by quantitative effectiveness targets and independent sampling
System Touchpoints: - Recall effectiveness analytics; POS block verification report; sample design tool

steps.activity: Product Safety Mgr defines effectiveness-check criteria (target recovery %, time-bound targets per regulator guidance) and sampling approach to verify customer reach
Data Analytics/Store Ops designs audit sample (stores, channels, customer segments) and verifies POS block, shelf removal, and notification delivery
Product Safety Mgr documents effectiveness results; identifies gaps; drives corrective follow-up before regulator close-out

fields.Participants: Inventory Control, DC Ops, Store Ops, Ecommerce, IT

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-reconcile of "reconciles quarantined quantities vs." (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-496 (ensure controlled execution — Recall Initiation, Risk Assessment & Regulatory Notification (PA-89.1).)
- operational: immediate system-wide block before physical quarantine
Pain Points / Risks: - **Leakage risk**: Stock sold after stop-sale decision; mitigated by immediate system-wide block before physical quarantine
System Touchpoints: - Inventory hold/quarantine status; POS item block; ecommerce/marketplace listing control (links to VS-10/VS-65); WMS recall bin

steps.activity: Inventory Control/IT places system-wide stop-sale (POS block, ecommerce/marketplace listing suspension, PO/replenishment freeze) on affected SKU/lot across all locations
DC Ops/Store Ops physically quarantine on-hand stock to segregated recall bin/area; apply recall hold labels; prevent sale or shipment
Inventory Control reconciles quarantined quantities vs. system stock; investigates variances; secures high-value/regulated goods under additional LP control

fields.Frequency: The rarest integrity-event class in the product-safety estate: years can pass chain-wide without a credible episode; the sweep-decision discipline is exercised through the W627 mock-recall rotation
fields.Participants: Recall Committee chair (W2997), VP Legal (extortion/no-ransom posture), Store Operations leadership (sweep task campaigns), Loss Prevention (evidence and W1337 law-enforcement coordination), Corporate Communications (W3001-class customer-communication discipline), HSE Manager (VS-24), Category Manager (affected SKUs), PNP anti-cybercrime / economic-crime units
fields.Trigger: A threat, extortion demand, or malicious claim that BuildRight merchandise on shelves has been or will be contaminated, tampered with, or booby-trapped — by call, letter, email, social post, or in-person note — with or without a money demand
fields.Volume: 1 event × the threat's claimed scope (a single SKU, a category, one store, or the whole chain) × the sweep surface (targeted SKU pulls at ~200 stores, hours to a full-day campaign if ordered) × the notification set (PNP assessment, DTI-BPS/FDA per W2995 where consumers are at risk, the W2997 committee)

workflows.name: Product-Tampering Threat, Extortion Demand & Merchandise-Integrity Sweep Protocol

Automation Opportunity: - Threat-case template with a built-in sweep-decision gate (assessment fields, decision, basis, approver) that must be completed before any W3000 stop-sale object can be raised from the case
- Auto-generated targeted store sweep task campaign on the credible path, with sample-pull and chain-of-custody forms attached (replaces manual store-by-store calls)
Background: VS-89 owns product-safety intake (W2993), the recall decision (W2994), regulatory notification (W2995), committee command (W2997), and stop-sale execution (W3000) — but every one of those triggers on a defect found or a vendor/regulator notice. 'Tampering threat'/'contamination threat'/'extortion' appear in zero dedicated headers anywhere: nobody owns the *threat* — the caller who claims needles in the cement bags unless paid, the letter claiming bleach was injected into a paint line — where the distinctive decisions are the never-pay rule, the specificity-gated sweep-or-monitor decision (the W5538 bomb-threat decision law transposed to merchandise: sweeping the whole chain on every vague threat trains extortionists and burns a full trading day across ~200 stores, while dismissing a specific one is the consumer-harm catastrophe), and the W3000 stop-sale canon executing only on the credible path. This workflow is that event owner; if altered product is actually found, W2994's recall machinery takes over and this protocol becomes its evidence and communications spine.
Controls: - CTL-496 (ensure controlled execution — Recall Initiation, Risk Assessment & Regulatory Notification (PA-89.1).)

- operational: never-pay rule with VP Legal sign-off recorded on the case; sweep/stop-sale decision and its documented basis precede execution; altered units preserved under chain of custody, never re-shelved
Pain Points / Risks: - **Panic-sweep risk**: a chain-wide stop-sale ordered on every vague threat trains extortionists and costs a full trading day across ~200 stores; mitigated by Step 4's specificity-gated decision documented before execution

- **Under-reaction risk**: dismissing a specific threat that proves real is the consumer-harm and RA 7394/DTI-enforcement catastrophe; mitigated by Step 3's mandatory law-enforcement assessment on every case
- **Evidence-destruction risk**: the letter discarded, the email deleted, or the inspected unit re-shelved destroys both the criminal case and the recall basis; mitigated by Step 1/5 custody rules
- **Admission-in-communication risk**: improvised statements implying prior knowledge of contamination; mitigated by Step 2/7 scripted-channel discipline
- **Copycat risk**: paying once, or visibly over-reacting once, invites the next demand; mitigated by the never-pay rule with VP Legal sign-off recorded on every case
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed by Product Safety & Compliance, the W2997 committee bench, and store task-campaign capacity; no incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - Threat/case log with evidence attachments and restricted visibility
- Stop-sale, quarantine, and POS block objects on the targeted-SKU path (links to W3000)
- Sample-pull task campaigns with chain-of-custody records (links to W63-class store task tooling)
- Regulatory notification objects (links to W2995) and recall-decision records (links to W2994)
- Customer-notice channels and script version control (links to W3001)
Time Estimate: Per event: ≈ 40–80 staff-hours over the first week (committee, legal, LP, store task campaigns) plus store sweep labor scaled to the targeted-SKU surface. Readiness rides the W627 mock rotation — no incremental headcount.

steps.activity: **Threat capture & preservation**: verbatim record of every contact attempt; caller-line capture, envelope, email headers, and screenshots preserved in the case file; if the caller is live, keep them talking without negotiating
steps.r: Store Manager / Contact-center Agent / LP Duty

steps.activity: **Posture decision — never pay, never improvise public statements**: VP Legal with Product Safety confirm the no-payment rule and route all public communication through the W3001 discipline (no confirmation, no denial, no speculation outside scripted channels)
steps.r: VP Legal / Product Safety & Compliance Manager

steps.activity: **Credibility assessment with law enforcement**: specificity of SKU/store/timing claimed, the claimant's knowledge of real product detail, prior-contact history, and platform metadata assessed jointly with PNP; the assessment feeds and is filed with the sweep decision
steps.r: Product Safety & Compliance Manager / LP Investigator

steps.activity: **Sweep-or-monitor decision (documented either way)**: specific and credible → targeted sweep/quarantine of the named SKUs via W3000 stop-sale and quarantine at affected sites; vague or not credible → heightened monitoring and sample pulls only — the decision and its basis recorded on the case before execution
steps.r: Product Safety & Compliance Manager / Recall Committee chair

steps.activity: **Physical verification & chain of custody**: sample units pulled and inspected for seal/pack integrity; laboratory testing where contamination is chemically plausible; any altered unit found is preserved as evidence, never re-shelved or destroyed
**Regulatory posture**: W2995 DTI-BPS/FDA notification where a credible contamination risk to consumers exists; if altered product is verified, the W2994 recall decision runs on this evidence
**Customer & store communication**: scripted, no-speculation customer guidance per W3001 if a sweep is public-visible; store briefing pack so counter staff never improvise answers

**Case file, hardening & recurrence watch**: packaging/sealing review on tamper-prone SKUs, camera coverage review on affected aisles, threat intelligence filed to W1337, and the episode folded into the W627 mock rotation
